s.t: On the very first UK independent singles chart, launched on 19 January 1980, the Mo-dettes were at No. 4 with it, above Dead Kennedys and Joy Division’s ‘Transmission’.
s.src: Official Charts: Celebrating 40 years of the Independent Singles Chart
s.q: a chart that focused entirely on independent acts was launched on January 19th 1980, published in Record Week. … The first Independent Singles Chart Top 10 … 4. Mo-dettes - White Mice / Masochistic Opposite 5. Dead Kennedys - California Uber Alles 6. Joy Division - Transmission

s.t: Rough Trade’s Scott Piering said in 1980 the Mo-dettes’ single would have ‘benefitted greatly’ from Radio 1’s daytime playlist, whose fourth-floor bosses indies couldn’t reach, unlike John Peel’s third.
s.q: while you can get to people like John Peel on the third, it is impossible for people like us to get to those on the fourth, who control the main daytime radio. … records like Spizz Energi's Where's Captain Kirk' or the Mo-dettes 'White Mice', which were pushed by independent pluggers … would have benefitted greatly from being on the playlist.

s.t: In January 1980, Record Mirror credited the Mo-dettes with ‘the best female rhythm section in the history of Women In Rock’ and called it one of Rough Trade’s best-ever releases.
s.q: MO-DETTES: 'White Mice' (Rough Trade) they have the best female rhythm section in the history of Women In Rock and a pleasant-voiced singer who is faintly reminiscent of Lene Lovich. … this is certainly one of Rough Trade's best-ever releases.

s.t: Sounds’ Garry Bushell said ‘White Mouse Disco’, the Mo-dettes’ rejigged remake on their album The Story So Far, ‘could and should have been number one for a summer season’.
s.src: Sounds, 8 November 1980 (album review by Garry Bushell)
s.q: And what could be more colourful than the glorious rejigged version of 'White Mice' included here as 'White Mouse Disco', … a high-sweeping pulsing classic of a pop song that could and should have been number one for a summer season.

s.t: Jane Crockford of the Mo-dettes wrote it, and it champions sexual autonomy, though the band were critical of partisan feminist politics; they released it themselves in mid-1979 on Mode Records.
s.q: Mo-dettes' best-known song is "White Mice", written by Jane Crockford, which was self-released as their first single in mid-1979 on Mode records, with "Masochistic Opposite" on the B-side. The song champions sexual autonomy, although the band members were critical of partisan feminist politics.

f.t: Lawyers refused them permission to use Rodgers and Hammerstein’s ‘My Favourite Things’ on their debut album, The Story So Far, because singer Ramona Carlier had twisted its words in French.
f.q: the ghost of Rodgers and Hammerstein has struck! Lawyers have refused permission for them to use 'My Favourite Things' on their debut elpee due to a slight twisting of the lyrics that Ramona sings in French.

f.t: At a 1976 Clash gig, bassist-to-be Jane Crockford was pictured with a bleeding Shane MacGowan; Joe Strummer said ‘Mad Jane’s teeth and Shane’s earlobe’ got the Clash in the papers.
f.src: Far Out: “These people are cannibals”: The Clash gig that helped launch Shane MacGowan
f.q: Featuring MacGowan and ‘Mad Jane’ Crockford, later of the Mo-dettes, they conveyed an image of pure punk carnage … MacGowan could be seen with blood pouring from his right ear … “Without Mad Jane’s teeth and Shane’s earlobe, we wouldn’t have got in the papers that week.”

f.t: In 1980 they had to cancel their British tour after a handful of gigs: drummer June Miles-Kingston had broken her toe by dropping a can of paint on it.
f.q: THE MO-DETTES have had to cancel their British tour after only a handful of gigs because drummer June Miles-Kingston broke her toe when she dropped a can of paint on it.

f.t: For their 1981 single ‘Tonight’, Decca wanted ‘traditional saccharine girl pop’, then a fuller sound: guitarist Melissa Ritter joined and played her first show four days later.
f.q: For this single, Decca Records had asked the band to alter their sound to "traditional saccharine girl pop" leading to some tension. Two months later, also at the request of Decca Records, who wanted to hear a fuller sound, Mo-dettes asked guitarist Melissa Ritter to join. She played her first show as a Mo-dette just four days after joining the band.

f.t: Billed as the Bomberettes, they sang the backing vocals on ‘Fighter Pilot’, on John Cale’s 1981 album Honi Soit.
f.q: Also in 1981, billed as Bomberettes, they provided backing vocals on the track "Fighter Pilot" on John Cale's album Honi Soit.
